Name: Foundation
Scope: Module scaffold, people schema, RBAC scaffolding, events/audit, org isolation
Acceptance: Module scaffolds, migrates, emits events with audit, and enforces org isolation before any feature builds on it

Name: Module foundation
Scope: Module scaffold, people schema base, inbound-event subscriber framework, events/audit, org isolation primitive (F-SEC-2, F-SEC-3); enabling, no user value
Acceptance: Empty people module scaffolds and migrates; person/employment_period/worker/worker_history tables exist; a tenant/session guard scopes the module's own queries so a seeded row in org A is never returned to an org-B session; the inbound-event subscriber framework is in place; domain events emit transactionally with audit recorded (per-feature query scoping is each feature slice's own acceptance)

Name: Identity link & first-login binding
Scope: Identity link & first-login binding; identity user.* projection (PRD section 3; identity to people)
Acceptance: A pre-provisioned person with no login exists; on first SSO sign-in the auth principal links to that existing person and never auto-creates one; a sign-in for someone not pre-provisioned is rejected

Name: People directory & records
Scope: F-WORK-1..11, F-DOC-1..2: employee record, pay/capacity, skills, documents, directory + projection, onboarding, import, assignment history, hire/re-hire
Acceptance: A person has one trusted, permission-aware record discoverable in the directory; HR creates and maintains people end to end

Name: Employee record & field-level edit
Scope: F-WORK-1, F-WORK-4 (edit + change history; effective-dated pay/capacity is out of scope here and lives in PPL-4)
Acceptance: A new record needs at least a full name; a unique work email is generated when none is supplied; personal details are editable by the person or an admin while position/grade/pay/bank/tax are admin-only; every change appears in the person's change history with who and when

Name: Effective-dated pay & capacity
Scope: F-WORK-4 pay history, F-WORK-8 capacity; owns the effective-dating primitive (no-overlap, future-dating)
Acceptance: Changing pay or capacity adds a new effective-dated record rather than overwriting; past periods still read at the old value; a change can be future-dated; overlapping effective ranges are rejected

Name: Skills
Acceptance: A person holds several catalog skills each at proficiency 0-5 with optional years; a skill not in the catalog cannot be added; a skill may be backed by a certification with an expiry and the person is flagged when it lapses; a position can carry a required-skills baseline

Name: Document vault
Scope: F-DOC-1, F-DOC-2 vault + document-requirement policy + expiry
Acceptance: Documents upload with optional expiry and replace in place keeping prior versions in history; the document-requirement policy (overall or by employment type) is configurable and a person missing a required document is flagged; documents nearing expiry remind HR and the owner

Name: Directory views, search & filter
Scope: F-WORK-5 directory, search, filter + suite search
Acceptance: The directory shows as cards or a list, searches by name/role/email/skill as the user types, and filters by lifecycle stage (and by account once allocation data is present); an empty result shows a clear no-matching-people state; results are scoped to the viewer by tier and reporting line, with allocation/account-based visibility added once PPL-40 lands; the same search backs the suite-wide search bar

Name: Onboard a person
Acceptance: A Strategic user adds a member via a short form; on save the person is created at the start of the journey, an employee ID is assigned, the entered manager seeds the position and reporting line, and a workspace-account request is logged as a placeholder for manual action

Name: Bulk import
Acceptance: A spreadsheet is validated against the expected columns; rows missing a required value are skipped and reported while valid rows import; imported rows land only in the caller's org; the user sees valid-vs-rejected counts before and after

Name: Effective-dated job history
Scope: F-WORK-11 effective-dated assignment history (reuses the PPL-4 effective-dating primitive)
Acceptance: Every assignment change (position, org unit, grade, reporting line) is one dated record with a reason; a person's position and grade are queryable as of any past date; a future-dated change shows as scheduled and takes effect on its date

Name: Create employee from a hire
Summary: PPL-11 Create employee from a hire
Scope: F-WORK-9 create employee from a hire
Acceptance: When Hiring marks a candidate hired, an employee record is created from the candidate's details with nothing re-typed, linked to the funded position, starting at Preboarding/Onboarding; HR can complete it before start; a candidate who was not hired never becomes an employee

Name: Re-hire a former employee
Acceptance: A returning person matched at hire (by identity, work email, or name + date of birth) gets a new employment period on the same person with prior history intact and the original hire date preserved; no duplicate record; a genuine new person gets a new record

Name: Worker directory read-model
Scope: rm_worker_directory event-maintained projection (enabling; replaces the live join-view)
Acceptance: Worker, lifecycle and capacity events maintain a directory projection carrying name/email/lifecycle_stage/grade/fte/department, idempotent on event id; re-delivering an event yields no duplicate; it answers directory search and filter without a live cross-table join and never returns rows outside the viewer's org

Name: Org structure & positions
Scope: F-ORG-1..3: org units, positions, org chart
Acceptance: The org is modelled as nested units and single-holder positions, and rendered as a scoped, drill-in org chart

Name: Org units & positions
Scope: F-ORG-1, F-ORG-2 org units (acyclic), positions, assign/vacate single-holder
Acceptance: A Strategic user builds nested org units (cycles rejected) and defines positions bound to role and grade; a position is open or filled and holds at most one person; assigning a holder marks it filled and vacating marks it open

Name: Org chart
Acceptance: Anyone sees an org chart at company, account, or project level with zoom, pan, and drill-in from an account to its projects; reporting lines come from positions, not a typed manager field; only the parts of the org the viewer may see are shown

Name: Resource allocation & utilization
Scope: F-ALLOC-1..3: read-only allocation & utilization from PM + supporting projections
Acceptance: People surfaces who is allocated where and how loaded, read-only and scoped, degrading gracefully when PM or the timesheet feed is down

Name: Allocation read-model
Scope: rm_allocation projection from PM assignment events (enabling; drives RBAC visibility)
Acceptance: PM assignment events build a store-only allocation read-model in people holding per-person/project/account percentage by date; re-delivering the same assignment event twice yields exactly one allocation row; the projection answers who-is-allocated-where as of a date

Name: Allocation view
Acceptance: A user sees who is allocated to which projects and accounts by month with a per-person and per-account breakdown, read-only; a person on several projects sums across them; the view is scoped to the viewer and shows unavailable rather than wrong numbers when PM is down

Name: Utilization
Acceptance: Each person's utilization shows planned vs actual split into billable/internal/bench/leave (read from PM, which owns the computation); anyone over 100% in a month is flagged over-allocated; figures degrade to unavailable or last-known when PM is down; the actual figure is omitted (not guessed) when the timesheet feed is absent

Name: Account/project read-model
Scope: rm_account_project projection from PM (enabling; account/project id-to-name for labels & filters)
Acceptance: PM account/project events maintain an id-to-name account-project projection, idempotent on event id, so People can label allocations and filter the directory by account without a cross-module query

Name: Workforce analytics
Scope: F-ANALYTICS-1..2: workforce dashboard, forecast, skills picture + metrics projection
Acceptance: Leaders turn workforce data into decisions through a scoped dashboard, forward-looking forecasts, and a skills/talent picture against demand

Name: Workforce dashboard (current state)
Acceptance: A leader sees a workforce dashboard of current-state metrics (headcount, utilization, attrition-to-date, bench, tenure, seniority, skill coverage and gaps, critical-role coverage) scoped to what they manage (org-wide, account, team, or self)

Name: Skills & talent picture
Acceptance: A user sees the organization's skills broken down by seniority band against where skills are in demand, with search and paging, scoped to the viewer

Name: Workforce metrics read-model
Acceptance: Worker, lifecycle, capacity, skill and allocation events maintain a metrics projection (headcount, attrition, bench, tenure, skill coverage) by scope and period, idempotent on event id, so the dashboard reads pre-aggregated figures rather than scanning base tables

Name: Headcount & attrition forecast
Acceptance: The dashboard shows forward-looking hiring and attrition forecasts and turnover/exit projections derived from lifecycle and offboarding history, scoped to what the leader manages; when source history is insufficient the forecast shows as unavailable rather than guessed

Name: Headcount planning
Acceptance: Strategic users budget positions per org unit and period and compare planned against filled, feeding the single demand pipeline

Name: Headcount plan
Acceptance: A Strategic user sets budgeted positions for an org unit in a period and sees planned-vs-filled; an open or vacated budgeted position emits people.position.opened so PM raises the one-seat backfill, rather than People raising a separate, parallel hiring signal

Name: Lifecycle directory & dashboard
Acceptance: Every employee carries a stage on a guarded state machine, browsable by stage and surfaced as a per-tier dashboard with an attention list

Name: Lifecycle stage machine
Scope: F-LIFE-1, F-WORK-7 lifecycle stage machine (sole owner of F-WORK-7)
Acceptance: Every employee carries a lifecycle stage (Preboarding to Onboarding to Probation to Active to Offboarding to Alumni, plus On leave and Did not start); only valid transitions are allowed and an illegal change (e.g. reopening an Alumni as Active) is rejected; each transition is recorded in the person's lifecycle/change history and emits a lifecycle event

Name: Lifecycle directory
Acceptance: A user browses everyone by stage with filters by stage and department; each row shows stage, progress, a plain health label (On track/At risk/Blocked/Overdue/Complete), manager, and next milestone, and opens that person's journey; the directory is scoped to the viewer

Name: Lifecycle dashboard
Acceptance: Each tier sees a fitting dashboard: leadership gets stage funnels, trends, department comparisons and a risk heatmap; a manager sees their team; a member sees their own stage, progress, tasks and documents; overdue and blocked items surface as an attention list that jumps to the record

Name: Onboarding
Scope: F-ONB-1..5: onboarding, IT handoff, preboarding, rescind/no-show
Acceptance: A new hire is brought on board through an owner-laned checklist, with IT handoff, a self-service preboarding lane, and a clean did-not-start path

Name: Onboarding process & board
Acceptance: Onboarding runs a multi-phase checklist (pre-onboarding to day to post) with each step owned by HR/IT/Lead/C&B, viewable as a board or a per-person checklist with a completion ring; moving a card or ticking items advances work, a blocked step must be resolved before continuing, and on completion the person advances out of onboarding and HR, their manager and IT are notified

Name: IT handoff
Acceptance: IT-owned onboarding steps (laptop, email/Teams, group mail, VPN/SSO, toolset) can be handed to the IT service desk from a pre-filled request

Name: Preboarding lane & day-1 readiness
Acceptance: A new hire has a preboarding task lane (confirm details, sign and upload documents, acknowledge equipment) distinct from the HR/IT/Lead lanes; what they submit is held for HR to confirm; day-1 readiness is a visible milestone and the person becomes Active only once onboarding completes

Name: Rescind / no-show before start
Acceptance: A hire who withdraws before day one or no-shows at onboarding is closed as Did not start (not Alumni) with a reason, and the filled project seat reopens in PM so the backfill resumes

Name: Probation
Acceptance: A probationer is reviewed at scheduled checkpoints (input vs decision separated) and confirmed, extended, or not confirmed by HR

Name: Probation reviews
Acceptance: A person in probation has scheduled checkpoints (e.g. 1-month, 2-month, and a confirmation around 90 days) capturing a 1-5 score and reviewer note against weighted objectives with progress and a risk indicator; a Team Lead/EM submits review input but cannot decide the outcome

Name: Confirmation decision
Acceptance: At probation end HR records Pass & confirm (person becomes Active), Extend (a new confirmation date, repeatable, org-default length adjustable), or Do not confirm (offboarding begins); the decision records who and when; a Do-not-confirm signals PM exit-pending at the moment it is taken

Name: Movement
Scope: F-MOVE-1..3: movement request, approval, effective-date apply, mobility inbound
Acceptance: A job change is one record (promotion, transfer, or pay) routed through a single approval chain and applied on its effective date, whether started in People or arriving from Hiring

Name: Movement request & approval
Acceptance: A Manager or AM proposes a promotion, transfer, or pay change for someone they manage stating from/to and an effective date; it runs the single canonical approval chain (a pay change skips leader review); any approver can reject or send back, and a rejected move does not take effect and its outcome is recorded

Name: Apply on effective date
Acceptance: An approved move applies on its effective date (not at approval) exactly once, re-binding the position and adding a dated pay record; any allocation change is committed through PM; the person is notified and a Hiring-originated move closes its originating application

Name: Internal-mobility inbound move
Acceptance: An internal-mobility selection approved in Hiring arrives already PMO-capacity-approved and is recorded as a movement against the existing person (never a new hire); HR applies the people-policy aspect and does not re-approve capacity

Name: Offboarding
Acceptance: A leaver runs an owner-laned clearance workflow that revokes access, returns assets, and ends in Alumni with PM allocations closed

Name: Offboarding process & lanes
Acceptance: Offboarding runs a clearance workflow (Receive information to Prepare to Execute to Complete) with parallel HR/Lead/IT/Finance lanes; a leaver is marked voluntary or involuntary with progress, health, last day and reason; it can be put on hold or cancelled before completion, returning the person to their prior stage

Name: Deactivation, clearance & completion
Acceptance: IT and Finance steps cover access removal and asset return via a pre-filled service-desk request; for an involuntary exit access is revoked immediately rather than on the last day; when all lanes finish the person becomes Alumni, the record is retained per policy, parties are notified, and PM is signalled to end any open allocations

Name: Performance
Acceptance: Performance runs on a versioned weighted scorecard through recurring cycles with goals/OKRs, calibrated across teams and able to seed a move

Name: Scorecard instrument & rules
Acceptance: A review uses a weighted scorecard of criteria grouped into pillars; core criteria are mandatory, an extreme 1 or 5 requires written evidence, and any criterion below 4 requires a top action; a guided maturity self-assessment feeds one criterion; a completed review keeps the criteria and weights it was scored against so re-weighting later never shifts past results

Name: Review cycles & goals/OKRs
Acceptance: HR runs recurring review cycles with per-person goals/OKRs (objective, key results, weight, progress) set by managers and the people themselves; My Scorecard and Team Evaluation views show the previous period for comparison; closing a cycle finalizes its reviews

Name: Calibration & promotion-from-review
Acceptance: Before a cycle closes, managers' ratings can be calibrated to normalize scores across teams and the calibrated result is finalized; a strong review outcome can seed a promotion or pay-change movement directly from the review

Name: Time-off / Leave
Scope: F-LEAVE-1: leave proxy to the timesheet system
Acceptance: People surfaces leave balances and submits requests through the timesheet system, owning no leave data

Name: Leave balance & request
Acceptance: A person sees their leave balance and submits a request from within People, both handled by the timesheet system; People stores no leave data; if the timesheet system is unavailable the balance shows unavailable and a request is held until it can be submitted

Name: Access control & data protection
Scope: F-SEC-1, F-SEC-4: sensitive-data protection, scope derivation, cross-account grant
Acceptance: Who sees whom is derived from tier, reporting line and live allocation, sensitive fields are masked and re-checked at request, and cross-account access is granted, never self-set

Name: Sensitive-field masking & tier visibility
Acceptance: Pay, bank and tax show as Restricted to anyone who is not the record owner or a Strategic user and are editable only by Strategic; visibility otherwise follows tier and the reporting line derived from positions (Member sees self, Manager sees direct reports, Strategic sees all)

Name: Allocation-driven scope & at-request re-check
Scope: F-SEC-1 allocation-driven scope + synchronous at-request re-check
Acceptance: A manager also sees the people allocated to projects they manage and a person on two accounts is visible to both account managers; sensitive-data access is re-checked at the moment of request by re-validating an active allocation synchronously against PM (not the lagging read-model), so the very next request after an allocation ends is refused with no stale window

Name: Cross-account access grant
Acceptance: An Account Manager can request access to an account they don't own; a PMO or Strategic user grants or revokes it (never self-granted); a grant widens visibility to that account across People, Hiring and PM for its duration and revoking removes it everywhere immediately; both are audited

Name: Assistant tools
Acceptance: Ask Seta can read what the user may see and draft changes, each held for human approval before save

Name: Read & draft-approve tools
Acceptance: The assistant reads only what the current user may see and drafts changes (onboard someone, update a field, start an offboarding, record an evaluation); every drafted change is held for the user to approve before it is saved, and it never reads or changes anything the user couldn't themselves
